claims.disproof_condition: Lower substitutability if another US NdPr producer reaches sustained commercial production (e.g., a development-stage project completes ramp), or if a US magnet maker demonstrates scaled output with non-MP feedstock; raise toward 5 only with customer-side evidence that qualified alternatives failed.
claims.statement: For US-domiciled sourcing of NdPr feedstock and the magnets built on it, MP Materials is per FAS the only active domestic producer of NdPr with all other projects still in development, while China processes 91% of all rare earth elements globally. Substitutability judged 4/5 (not 5): Chinese supply exists for buyers without domestic-sourcing constraints, and US magnet alternatives (recyclers, new entrants) are in development but not at commercial scale per the same source.

source_doc.title: Unpacking the DoD and MP Materials Partnership — MP uniqueness excerpts

sources.quote: A new multibillion dollar partnership between DoD and MP Materials, the only active domestic producer of NdPr, announced on July 10th, seems to be the agency's big bet on a solution.
One argument for MP Materials is that they are the only currently operating producer of NdPr—all the other projects are still in development—so this was the least risky investment option for DoD.

Rare earth elements have been the primary target of critical minerals trade tensions between the United States and the People's Republic of China (PRC), which processes 91% of all rare earth elements globally.
